world.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes on industry and refineries
world.summary: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Ukrainian industrial sites on Sept. 22, using missiles, drones and artillery to strike Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad in the Dnipropetrovsk region. Ukrainian regional officials said three people were killed and six wounded in Dnipro, where warehouses and a business were bad
world.content: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Ukrainian industrial sites on Sept. 22, using missiles, drones and artillery to strike Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad in the Dnipropetrovsk region. Ukrainian regional officials said three people were killed and six wounded in Dnipro, where warehouses and a business were badly damaged. Strikes also hit Kyiv and industrial or critical-infrastructure sites in other regions. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 212 drones alongside several types of missiles, while air defenses reported neutralizing 186 aerial targets. Ukraine also attacked Russia’s Samara region, where a fire was reported at Rosneft’s Kuibyshev refinery after what the regional governor described as a drone assault on industrial facilities. The governor reported no casualties but said homes, cars and other civilian property were damaged. The attacks followed Ukraine’s Sept. 20 mass drone raid on Moscow, which damaged the Moscow refinery. Reuters sources said both main crude-distillation units caught fire and processing stopped, with repairs potentially taking several weeks.
world.image_alt: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes on industry and refineries

world.title: Macron and Trump discuss Ukraine energy truce, Hormuz access
world.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron met U.S. President Donald Trump in New York on Monday, Sept. 21, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. Macron said they discussed the war in Ukraine, Red Sea security and measures to ease pressure on energy markets. He said they considered steps to protect oil facilit
world.content: French President Emmanuel Macron met U.S. President Donald Trump in New York on Monday, Sept. 21, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. Macron said they discussed the war in Ukraine, Red Sea security and measures to ease pressure on energy markets. He said they considered steps to protect oil facilities in the Red Sea and a mutual moratorium on strikes against Ukrainian and Russian energy infrastructure. Macron pressed for faster, larger deliveries of missile interceptors to Ukraine, calling them a defensive priority. He said France and the United States would work together to protect critical infrastructure in the Middle East and ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. France is considering a United Nations Security Council resolution on navigation through the strait. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was scheduled to meet Trump in New York on Sept. 22 and planned to advocate an energy truce with Russia.
world.image_alt: Macron and Trump discuss Ukraine energy truce, Hormuz access

world.title: China expels two top generals over disloyalty allegations
world.summary: China expelled Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Communist Party and the military, accusing them of disloyalty, corruption and serious disciplinary violations, according to an official announcement on Sept. 21. Zhang was senior vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, China’s top military command body, whil
world.content: China expelled Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Communist Party and the military, accusing them of disloyalty, corruption and serious disciplinary violations, according to an official announcement on Sept. 21. Zhang was senior vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, China’s top military command body, while Liu served on the commission and led its Joint Staff Department. Zhang had been regarded as President Xi Jinping’s closest military ally. Chinese leaders said the two men formed cliques, violated political discipline, abused their positions and failed to supervise staff and relatives. Official documents also alleged that political and economic misconduct were intertwined and involved exceptionally large sums. Authorities began investigations in January and removed both men from the commission in late August, before announcing the expulsions. Their cases were referred to the military procuratorate for prosecution.
world.image_alt: China expels two top generals over disloyalty allegations

world.title: Houthis seize Yemen coast as Trump halts planned strikes
world.summary: Houthi fighters moved Monday to capture the Kahboub Mountains in Yemen’s Taiz and Lahij provinces, seeking to separate the Red Sea coast from territory held by Saudi-backed government forces. The advance followed the group’s seizure this month of much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, including the port of Mocha, and broug
world.content: Houthi fighters moved Monday to capture the Kahboub Mountains in Yemen’s Taiz and Lahij provinces, seeking to separate the Red Sea coast from territory held by Saudi-backed government forces. The advance followed the group’s seizure this month of much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, including the port of Mocha, and brought its forces closer to the Bab al-Mandab strait, a major shipping route. The New York Times reported that President Donald Trump halted planned U.S. airstrikes against the Houthis on Sunday after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman urged American intervention. Commanders had approved target lists and personnel were loading munitions, although Reuters said it could not independently verify the report. Yemen’s internationally recognized government also requested U.S. military assistance during a Sunday call between Trump and President Rashad al-Alimi, but sources said Trump made no direct commitment.
world.image_alt: Houthis seize Yemen coast as Trump halts planned strikes

world.title: President Trump pursues Belarus potash deal to replace Canada
world.summary: President Trump said Sept. 21 that the United States is working on a “massive” deal to buy potash from Belarus at a price substantially below what the United States pays Canada, which supplies most U.S. potash imports. Trump did not disclose the proposed volume, value, delivery schedule or whether Belarus had formally
world.content: President Trump said Sept. 21 that the United States is working on a “massive” deal to buy potash from Belarus at a price substantially below what the United States pays Canada, which supplies most U.S. potash imports. Trump did not disclose the proposed volume, value, delivery schedule or whether Belarus had formally agreed to the arrangement. The announcement followed an escalating U.S.-Canada trade dispute and could expand commercial ties with Belarus, a close Russian ally whose government has repressed dissidents and supported Russia’s war against Ukraine. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko said hours before Trump’s announcement that his country had no spare volume for Western markets because its output was already contracted and exports had shifted eastward. Washington has eased sanctions on Belarusian potash during negotiations involving the release of political prisoners, while the European Union continues to prohibit imports of Belarusian potash.
world.image_alt: President Trump pursues Belarus potash deal to replace Canada

world.title: UK charges Rwandan doctor over 1994 genocide allegations
world.summary: British prosecutors charged Dr Vincent Brown, formerly known as Vincent Bajinya, in London on Sept. 21 with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six counts of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity. The 65-year-old Rwandan who lives in north London is the first person charged in the United Ki
world.content: British prosecutors charged Dr Vincent Brown, formerly known as Vincent Bajinya, in London on Sept. 21 with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six counts of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity. The 65-year-old Rwandan who lives in north London is the first person charged in the United Kingdom over the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Prosecutors allege that he directed and incited others to commit murders and genocide in Kigali’s Rugenge district in April 1994. The Metropolitan Police War Crimes Team opened its investigation in September 2019 after a formal request from Rwanda. The Crown Prosecution Service said it authorised the charges after reviewing police evidence and determining that the legal test for prosecution had been met; Brown was held in custody and scheduled to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Sept. 22.
world.image_alt: UK charges Rwandan doctor over 1994 genocide allegations

world.title: G7 demands Houthis halt attacks on Saudi Arabia, urges Iran to end support
world.summary: G7 foreign ministers on Monday urged Yemen’s Houthis to immediately halt military operations, threats and attacks on civilian shipping, and return to political talks. They also called on Iran to stop arming and supporting the group, saying the escalation threatens regional and global energy security, international trad
world.content: G7 foreign ministers on Monday urged Yemen’s Houthis to immediately halt military operations, threats and attacks on civilian shipping, and return to political talks. They also called on Iran to stop arming and supporting the group, saying the escalation threatens regional and global energy security, international trade and economic stability. The statement followed a meeting in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, before Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was due to address the gathering. The appeal followed a Houthi offensive along Yemen’s Red Sea coast that reached areas near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, as well as continued attacks on Saudi Arabia. Houthi-linked media said Saudi strikes on the port city of Mokha killed at least six people and wounded eight. Iran denies supplying weapons to the Houthis and says its support is political.
world.image_alt: G7 demands Houthis halt attacks on Saudi Arabia, urges Iran to end support

world.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
world.summary: British Columbia filed a lawsuit in San Francisco federal court against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to alert law enforcement after its safety team flagged ChatGPT activity linked to the February 10 shooting in Tumbler Ridge. The province says the attack could have been prevented if OpenAI had
world.content: British Columbia filed a lawsuit in San Francisco federal court against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to alert law enforcement after its safety team flagged ChatGPT activity linked to the February 10 shooting in Tumbler Ridge. The province says the attack could have been prevented if OpenAI had warned police and is seeking damages for recovery costs, as well as court-ordered changes to how the company handles conversations that may signal violent threats. The attack killed eight people, including six children. The 18-year-old shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, bringing the death toll to nine. British Columbia alleges that OpenAI deactivated an account after internal safety reviewers identified violent content but did not contact authorities; the shooter then continued using a second account. The province also says OpenAI rejected requests to disclose the conversations. The Guardian reported that Altman apologized but did not implement promised reforms.
world.image_alt: British Columbia sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting

business.title: ECB launches Pontes for tokenized asset settlement
business.summary: The European Central Bank and euro-area national central banks launched Pontes on Sept. 21, a wholesale settlement system that allows eligible financial institutions to settle transactions in tokenized stocks, bonds and other assets in central-bank money. Pontes links distributed-ledger market platforms to the Eurosyst
business.content: The European Central Bank and euro-area national central banks launched Pontes on Sept. 21, a wholesale settlement system that allows eligible financial institutions to settle transactions in tokenized stocks, bonds and other assets in central-bank money. Pontes links distributed-ledger market platforms to the Eurosystem’s TARGET Services, providing an alternative to commercial-bank money, stablecoins and other private settlement instruments. Thirteen institutions have completed onboarding, including Deutsche Bank, Santander, Société Générale, KfW, the European Investment Bank, Clearstream and other market-infrastructure and ledger operators. The ECB has also begun preparing to invest a small part of its own-funds portfolio in tokenized, euro-denominated public-sector and supranational securities. The Executive Board will decide the timing and operational details after the preparatory work is complete. Pontes is separate from the retail digital euro, for which a one-year pilot is planned to begin in the second half of 2027, with possible issuance in 2029.
business.image_alt: ECB launches Pontes for tokenized asset settlement

business.title: Asian stocks rise as tech rally offsets rate concerns
business.summary: Asian stocks rose on Tuesday, September 22, after a technology-led rally on Wall Street. Lower oil prices and easing U.S. Treasury yields also supported risk appetite. Investors watched expected talks between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington later this week, including possible cooperation
business.content: Asian stocks rose on Tuesday, September 22, after a technology-led rally on Wall Street. Lower oil prices and easing U.S. Treasury yields also supported risk appetite. Investors watched expected talks between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington later this week, including possible cooperation on artificial intelligence and an extension of a trade truce. The gains came as investors bet the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates further to contain inflation, supporting the dollar. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose more than 1% in early trading, while South Korean stocks gained nearly 2% and Taiwan shares rose 1.3%. Japan’s markets were closed for a holiday. Brent crude steadied at $100.22 a barrel after falling more than 3% in the previous session.
business.image_alt: Asian stocks rise as tech rally offsets rate concerns

business.title: UK borrowing rises to £18.3bn ahead of Healey
business.summary: The UK government borrowed £18.3 billion in August, 19% more than a year earlier and £3.5 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecast, according to the Office for National Statistics. The figure was also higher than the £15.6 billion forecast by City analysts and was the second-highest borrowing total
business.content: The UK government borrowed £18.3 billion in August, 19% more than a year earlier and £3.5 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecast, according to the Office for National Statistics. The figure was also higher than the £15.6 billion forecast by City analysts and was the second-highest borrowing total for an August on record, behind 2020. Higher spending on public services, benefits and other costs outpaced increased tax receipts as inflation raised government outlays. Debt-interest payments reached £8.8 billion, the highest August figure since records began in 1997. Borrowing for the financial year to date reached £77.3 billion, £8.1 billion above the OBR’s forecast.
business.image_alt: UK borrowing rises to £18.3bn ahead of Healey

business.title: US diesel hits $6.51 as global supply crunch deepens
business.summary: The U.S. national average for diesel reached a record $6.5107 a gallon on Sept. 21, up from $6.23 a week earlier and $5.58 a month earlier, according to AAA. The price was about 76% higher than a year earlier as disruptions linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine reduced crude and refined-fuel flows and damaged refineri
business.content: The U.S. national average for diesel reached a record $6.5107 a gallon on Sept. 21, up from $6.23 a week earlier and $5.58 a month earlier, according to AAA. The price was about 76% higher than a year earlier as disruptions linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine reduced crude and refined-fuel flows and damaged refineries. The shortage is expected to persist into 2027. U.S. diesel inventories stood at 107.9 million barrels on Sept. 11, the lowest level for that point in the calendar year since EIA records began in 1982, while EIA projections show distillate stocks falling below 100 million barrels during September and remaining below the five-year low through most of 2027. Middle East diesel exports averaged 800,000 barrels per day from March through August, half their year-earlier level.
business.image_alt: US diesel hits $6.51 as global supply crunch deepens

business.title: Merz vows reforms after CDU’s historic election defeats
business.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he would remain in office and continue his economic and social reform program after the center-right Christian Democratic Union suffered its worst regional election result since the postwar period. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU won 4.9% and failed to clear the 5% thresh
business.content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he would remain in office and continue his economic and social reform program after the center-right Christian Democratic Union suffered its worst regional election result since the postwar period. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU won 4.9% and failed to clear the 5% threshold required for seats in the state parliament for the first time in modern Germany; the far-right Alternative for Germany won 38.2%. In Berlin, the CDU finished behind the Left Party, while the AfD also gained support. Merz said the governing coalition with the center-left Social Democratic Party would remain together and argued that Germany needs reforms to revive its economy. The results increased pressure on Merz as coalition partners and CDU figures debate whether to change the reform agenda, while negotiations over the European Union’s next seven-year budget face a year-end deadline.
business.image_alt: Merz vows reforms after CDU’s historic election defeats

business.title: Volkswagen exits Euro Stoxx 50 after profit warning
business.summary: Volkswagen was removed from the Euro Stoxx 50 at the market open on September 21, ending the German automaker’s 15-year membership in the eurozone’s benchmark index of large listed companies. In its annual review, Stoxx replaced Volkswagen with Nokia, added Engie and removed Wolters Kluwer. The change followed a declin
business.content: Volkswagen was removed from the Euro Stoxx 50 at the market open on September 21, ending the German automaker’s 15-year membership in the eurozone’s benchmark index of large listed companies. In its annual review, Stoxx replaced Volkswagen with Nokia, added Engie and removed Wolters Kluwer. The change followed a decline in Volkswagen’s free-float market value below the index’s qualifying threshold; index-tracking funds must sell holdings when constituents are removed. The removal followed Volkswagen’s September 18 warning that about €10 billion in one-off charges would reduce its 2026 operating margin to no more than 1%, from its previous forecast of 4%-5.5%. Volkswagen attributed the warning to a Porsche-related impairment, worsening market conditions, particularly in China, restructuring expenses and a faster-than-expected shift toward battery-electric vehicles. Volkswagen shares had fallen almost 30% this year and were trading near €76 at the time of reporting, close to a 16-year low.
business.image_alt: Volkswagen exits Euro Stoxx 50 after profit warning

business.title: Fed officials warn inflation fight may require higher rates
business.summary: Federal Reserve officials Austan Goolsbee and Alberto Musalem said the central bank may need to raise interest rates further to bring inflation back to its 2% target, warning that the effort could weaken employment and economic activity. Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said persistent supply
business.content: Federal Reserve officials Austan Goolsbee and Alberto Musalem said the central bank may need to raise interest rates further to bring inflation back to its 2% target, warning that the effort could weaken employment and economic activity. Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said persistent supply shocks, including higher oil prices linked to the Iran war and tariffs, have made it harder to wait for inflation to ease without tighter policy. Musalem, president of the St. Louis Fed, said persistent demand and recurring supply pressures made inflation more likely to remain substantially above target in 18 months without additional tightening. The Fed last week raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage point to a range of 3.75%-4%. Its preferred inflation gauge rose 3.7% in July from a year earlier.
business.image_alt: Fed officials warn inflation fight may require higher rates

business.title: US President Trump and Xi seek trade truce extension
business.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit Washington from Sept. 23 to 25 for talks with President Trump, including a formal summit on Sept. 24. Trade will be central as both governments seek to extend a tariff truce due to expire in November. Artificial intelligence, semiconductor restrictions, critical minerals, Taiwan
business.content: Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit Washington from Sept. 23 to 25 for talks with President Trump, including a formal summit on Sept. 24. Trade will be central as both governments seek to extend a tariff truce due to expire in November. Artificial intelligence, semiconductor restrictions, critical minerals, Taiwan and the war in Iran are also expected to be on the agenda. The meeting will be the leaders’ second face-to-face encounter this year and Xi’s first state visit to the United States since 2015. Neither side expects a comprehensive settlement. Washington wants trade and economic gains before the November midterm elections, while Beijing seeks more time and a continuation of the current arrangement. Officials and analysts said disputes over technology controls and Taiwan remain unresolved. Preparatory talks in New York involved Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Vice Premier He Lifeng and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.
business.image_alt: US President Trump and Xi seek trade truce extension

science.title: Study says small crustaceans probably built hexagonal fossil tunnels
science.summary: Researchers reviewing nearly perfect hexagonal fossil tunnels concluded that small crustaceans, which are arthropods, most likely created the structures rather than worm-like animals. The conclusion challenges a long-standing idea that a worm-like creature created the tunnels.
science.content: Researchers reviewing nearly perfect hexagonal fossil tunnels concluded that small crustaceans, which are arthropods, most likely created the structures rather than worm-like animals. The conclusion challenges a long-standing idea that a worm-like creature created the tunnels.
science.image_alt: Study says small crustaceans probably built hexagonal fossil tunnels

science.title: Stanford study finds brain develops from two cell systems
science.summary: A Stanford-led study published in Nature Neuroscience finds that the human brain develops from two distinct progenitor-cell systems rather than a shared developmental source. Researchers identified separate origins for the forebrain and midbrain, which support functions including language, reasoning and consciousness,
science.content: A Stanford-led study published in Nature Neuroscience finds that the human brain develops from two distinct progenitor-cell systems rather than a shared developmental source. Researchers identified separate origins for the forebrain and midbrain, which support functions including language, reasoning and consciousness, and the hindbrain, which regulates breathing, heartbeat, sleep, hunger, speaking and swallowing. Using mouse embryos, the team found that the two cell populations did not overlap and were marked by different genes, Otx2 and Gbx2. The researchers also used human pluripotent stem cells to produce functional hindbrain motor neurons, which they said could improve laboratory studies of brainstem diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and spinal muscular atrophy. The study’s senior author, Stanford neuroscientist Kyle Loh, said the two systems may have joined during evolution over hundreds of millions of years.
science.image_alt: Stanford study finds brain develops from two cell systems

science.title: Warming raises risk of glacier-triggered disasters after Nepal floods
science.summary: Scientists said human-caused warming played a very strong role in the Aug. 26 collapse that sent rock, ice, water and debris through Nepal and Tibet. The event killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing as of Sept. 16, according to Live Science; a separate UN-linked account said more than 1,200 peopl
science.content: Scientists said human-caused warming played a very strong role in the Aug. 26 collapse that sent rock, ice, water and debris through Nepal and Tibet. The event killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing as of Sept. 16, according to Live Science; a separate UN-linked account said more than 1,200 people had died. Researchers said warming destabilized permafrost and ice around the collapsed rock. They said rapidly shrinking glaciers and steep Himalayan terrain increase the risk of similar cascades. A large mass detached from a mountainside and fell about 2,000 meters into the Lhende River at roughly 150 meters per second, according to the Stimson Center as cited by Live Science. Experts said glacier-related slope failures can occur worldwide, including in tropical regions. World Weather Attribution researchers said the Himalayan freezing boundary is rising by about 100 meters each decade.
science.image_alt: Warming raises risk of glacier-triggered disasters after Nepal floods

science.title: Scientists find seven of nine planetary boundaries breached
science.summary: A 2026 Planetary Health Check led by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research found that seven of Earth’s nine planetary boundaries have exceeded the safe operating space, with each recording its highest level of transgression. The affected systems are climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, f
science.content: A 2026 Planetary Health Check led by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research found that seven of Earth’s nine planetary boundaries have exceeded the safe operating space, with each recording its highest level of transgression. The affected systems are climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, freshwater, biogeochemical flows, novel entities such as chemical pollutants, and ocean acidification. More than 60 scientists contributed to the assessment. Only stratospheric ozone depletion and atmospheric aerosol loading have improved over the past decade, although aerosol pollution remains unsafe in some regions. The researchers said crossing a boundary does not mean an Earth system has collapsed, but increases the risk of large-scale, persistent and potentially irreversible change. The report was released during New York Climate Week, after a year of record ocean heat, floods, wildfires and extreme heat.
science.image_alt: Scientists find seven of nine planetary boundaries breached

science.title: Bolivian researchers identify new wildcat species, Leopardus tilcayo
science.summary: Researchers have identified a previously unknown wildcat species in Bolivia’s Yungas cloud forests and named it Leopardus tilcayo, the first living cat species newly described in more than a century. A study published Sept. 17 in Current Biology analyzed 38 members of the South American Leopardus genus and found that a
science.content: Researchers have identified a previously unknown wildcat species in Bolivia’s Yungas cloud forests and named it Leopardus tilcayo, the first living cat species newly described in more than a century. A study published Sept. 17 in Current Biology analyzed 38 members of the South American Leopardus genus and found that animals collectively known as tiger cats comprise five species. The species came to researchers’ attention through Tigrino, a male estimated to be 10 years old. A Bolivian family initially mistook him for a domestic kitten before taking him to the Senda Verde Wildlife Sanctuary in 2017. Tigrino measures about 46 centimeters from head to tail base and weighs 1.4 kilograms. Little is known about the species’ biology, though scat containing small-rodent remains and camera-trap observations suggest it may prey on rodents and be active at night.
science.image_alt: Bolivian researchers identify new wildcat species, Leopardus tilcayo

science.title: Singing indris open mouths wider to project high notes
science.summary: Researchers at the universities of Turin and Warwick found that indris, Madagascar’s only known singing lemur, open their mouths wider as the pitch of their songs rises. The pattern resembles formant tuning used by trained opera singers, in which changes to the vocal tract help amplify particular frequencies and carry
science.content: Researchers at the universities of Turin and Warwick found that indris, Madagascar’s only known singing lemur, open their mouths wider as the pitch of their songs rises. The pattern resembles formant tuning used by trained opera singers, in which changes to the vocal tract help amplify particular frequencies and carry sound farther through dense rainforest. The team analysed 83 videos of 19 wild indris, using motion-tracking software to measure the positions of the animals’ upper and lower lips frame by frame and compare mouth opening with pitch. The study, published in PLOS Computational Biology on Sept. 21, examined a vocal adjustment associated with the indri’s long-distance communication, including group bonding and warnings to neighbouring groups.
science.image_alt: Singing indris open mouths wider to project high notes

science.title: Super El Niño breaks records months before expected peak
science.summary: A powerful El Niño has reached record or near-record intensity in the tropical Pacific months before its expected November-December peak. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region reached about 3.07C above average on Sept. 19, matching the 2015-16 record on one widely used measure. A separate NOAA-based
science.content: A powerful El Niño has reached record or near-record intensity in the tropical Pacific months before its expected November-December peak. Sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region reached about 3.07C above average on Sept. 19, matching the 2015-16 record on one widely used measure. A separate NOAA-based calculation put the central-Pacific rise at 3.05C, above the previous 3.02C high from late 2015. An average of 14 models analyzed by climatologist Zeke Hausfather projects a possible peak near 4C. The event has already been associated with drought, wildfires, disrupted fishing and water shortages from Central America to Indonesia. Forecasts indicate varying risks across Asia, Africa and the Americas. California Gov. Gavin Newsom declared a statewide emergency on Sept. 21, directing agencies to pre-position flood equipment and prepare roads and infrastructure for possible winter storms, flooding, landslides and coastal impacts.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño breaks records months before expected peak

science.title: Studies examine black hole feeding, jets and host galaxies
science.summary: Astronomers reported two findings on how supermassive black holes affect their surroundings and evolve across cosmic time. One study found evidence that black holes ranging from roughly 10 solar masses to supermassive scales launch powerful jets at the same point in their feeding cycles. A separate study used the James
science.content: Astronomers reported two findings on how supermassive black holes affect their surroundings and evolve across cosmic time. One study found evidence that black holes ranging from roughly 10 solar masses to supermassive scales launch powerful jets at the same point in their feeding cycles. A separate study used the James Webb Space Telescope to examine the environments of apparent supermassive-black-hole seeds in the early universe, when it was less than 1 billion years old. At high redshift, researchers found an abundance of galaxies hosting these candidate seeds, measuring the environments in which the earliest supermassive black holes formed.
science.image_alt: Studies examine black hole feeding, jets and host galaxies

sports.title: England captain Brook urges Carse to take time away
sports.summary: England white-ball captain Harry Brook said fast bowler Brydon Carse needed more time away from international cricket as he works through personal issues, despite being available for selection. Brook described Carse as a close friend and said he hoped the 31-year-old would eventually be ready to return. Carse has not a
sports.content: England white-ball captain Harry Brook said fast bowler Brydon Carse needed more time away from international cricket as he works through personal issues, despite being available for selection. Brook described Carse as a close friend and said he hoped the 31-year-old would eventually be ready to return. Carse has not appeared in an England squad since an August incident in Derby involving an alleged assault investigation. Derbyshire Police said on September 18 that its investigation had ended with no further action, but Carse remains under investigation by the independent Cricket Regulator. England head coach Brendon McCullum has said Carse must “get his house in order” before returning, while Carse has continued to play for Durham.
sports.image_alt: England captain Brook urges Carse to take time away

sports.title: Israel FA condemns Ireland manager over genocide comments
sports.summary: The Israel Football Association has condemned Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson after he said Ireland would be “playing against genocide” rather than “playing with Israel” in two upcoming UEFA Nations League matches. The IFA accused Hallgrimsson of “ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity” in a social-media po
sports.content: The Israel Football Association has condemned Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson after he said Ireland would be “playing against genocide” rather than “playing with Israel” in two upcoming UEFA Nations League matches. The IFA accused Hallgrimsson of “ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity” in a social-media post; the Football Association of Ireland has not publicly responded. The matches are scheduled for 27 September in Debrecen, Hungary, and 4 October in Backa Topola, Serbia, both on neutral grounds. More than 160 Irish sportspeople have called for a boycott, while protesters gathered outside the Ireland team’s Dublin hotel on 21 September. Ireland’s players have not publicly commented, and Hallgrimsson has said people within the squad are uncomfortable about the fixtures.
sports.image_alt: Israel FA condemns Ireland manager over genocide comments

sports.title: Liverpool monitor Feyenoord right-back Givairo Read amid rivals
sports.summary: Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right-back Givairo Read as they assess options at the position, with Arsenal and Manchester City also tracking the 20-year-old Netherlands Under-21 international. Read has helped Feyenoord remain unbeaten in the Eredivisie and has registered five assists in the opening weeks of the 20
sports.content: Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right-back Givairo Read as they assess options at the position, with Arsenal and Manchester City also tracking the 20-year-old Netherlands Under-21 international. Read has helped Feyenoord remain unbeaten in the Eredivisie and has registered five assists in the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign. Liverpool signed Jeremie Frimpong as Trent Alexander-Arnold's replacement in 2025, but reports say the Dutchman has struggled for consistency while Conor Bradley is injured. Ronald Araujo has filled in at right-back during a season-long loan from Barcelona that includes a €55 million (£47 million) option to buy. Signing Read could affect Liverpool's decision on Araujo's future. A move could come in the January transfer window, although reports describe Read as a longer-term target for 2027 and say no deal has been agreed.

sports.content: Shaun Edwards has joined England Women’s coaching staff as a consultant through the end of the WXV Global Series, the Rugby Football Union announced on September 21. The 59-year-old former rugby league international will work with head coach John Mitchell and defence coach Sarah Hunter, starting before England’s match against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Edwards left his role as France men’s defence coach in June after six years, following head coach Fabien Galthié’s restructuring of his backroom staff. England’s remaining WXV programme includes matches against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa, followed by the campaign finale against the United States in New Jersey on October 30.

sports.content: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after a foul ball struck him near the left cheekbone while he stood several feet in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds. The ball came off teammate Michael Busch’s check swing against Reds pitcher Luis Mey in the fourth inning. Bregman left the game and went to a hospital for X-rays and a CT scan. Bregman will not undergo surgery and hopes to return during the postseason, though the Cubs have not provided a recovery timetable. He returned to Chicago on Monday with his left eye swollen shut. The regular season has six games remaining, and the postseason begins September 29.

sports.content: Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka admitted obtaining a false Covid-19 vaccination certificate in 2022 while playing for Arsenal and apologized for what he called a mistake. The Lucerne public prosecutor’s office is investigating whether the certificate involved criminal conduct; Xhaka said he would cooperate fully with authorities. The Swiss Football Association and Xhaka jointly decided that he would not join the national-team camp or play in the next four Nations League matches. Switzerland’s fixtures during the international window include games against North Macedonia, Scotland and Slovenia. The federation said it would reassess the situation after the window.

The proposals will go before the F
sports.content: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has proposed an independent external review of the governing framework for major strategic initiatives, along with a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with the organisation’s 211 member associations, confederations and other stakeholders. The proposals will go before the FIFA Council at its meeting in Zurich on October 15. Possible changes to the roles of the president, bureau, council and congress are under discussion. Infantino made the proposal after FIFA abandoned the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan, which would have brought private investment into stakes in the World Cup and other competitions. He acknowledged that the plan became public before FIFA completed its institutional process, creating the impression that decisions had already been made. He said FIFA would not pursue the project and reiterated his commitment to leading the organisation.

Dart was hit by Rams defenders Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart as he released a third-down pass, landed awk
sports.content: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night’s 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after injuring his left knee on the seventh play of New York’s opening drive at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Dart was hit by Rams defenders Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart as he released a third-down pass, landed awkwardly and was later ruled out. Initial examinations indicated a sprained medial collateral ligament, while X-rays were negative. The Giants scheduled an MRI for Tuesday, September 22, to determine the injury’s full extent. Jameis Winston replaced Dart and completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception as New York finished with six points and 182 total yards. Giants general manager Joe Schoen said Dart would be okay, while coach John Harbaugh declined to confirm the diagnosis before further testing. Wide receiver Malik Nabers briefly left with a right shoulder injury but returned, while pass rusher Brian Burns and left tackle Andrew Thomas also exited later in the game with injuries.
